title: Get Power BI AI-Ready: The Secret Behind Next-Level Data Insights
summary: An unvetted third-party blog explains the 'Prep data for AI' workflow in Power BI: configuring an AI data schema, writing AI instructions, and setting verified answers so that Copilot gives more grounded responses, plus a testing/validation loop for confirming those changes actually take effect.
audience: Semantic model owners and report authors responsible for making a model reliably answerable by Copilot, and admins deciding whether/when to migrate away from the legacy Q&A visual.
why_it_matters: Copilot's answer quality depends directly on model preparation work that is easy to skip; the post also surfaces a firm, dated deadline (per Microsoft) for Q&A retirement, which is operationally relevant for anyone still relying on the legacy Q&A visual instead of Copilot.
takeaways: Power BI's 'Prep data for AI' dialog groups three distinct preparation tools: an AI data schema, free-text AI instructions, and verified-answer pinning on specific visuals.

Renaming fields and adding column/measure descriptions specifically improves how Copilot interprets ambiguous business terminology, since only a limited amount of each description is actually read by Copilot.
Documenting every single column indiscriminately is called out as a practitioner antipattern that produces shallow, low-value descriptions rather than better answers.
Changes made through Prep data for AI are not instantaneous; the post recommends a wait-and-retest workflow before concluding a change didn't work.
Per Microsoft's own documentation, the classic Q&A visual is being retired, which is presented as the forcing function for migrating preparation effort toward Copilot instead.

claims.text: Power BI's Prep data for AI dialog is a single unified entry point exposing three separate preparation tools for a semantic model: an AI data schema, free-text AI instructions, and verified answers.

Configuring the AI data schema involves renaming cryptic technical field names to business-friendly terms, adding descriptions to key measures and columns, supplying business-vocabulary synonyms, and flagging fields as analytical focus points such as date dimensions or core KPIs.

Effective AI instructions cover business terminology and acronyms, temporal context such as fiscal-year definitions, default filtering assumptions, and disambiguation rules for similar concepts that span multiple tables.

A verified answer is set by selecting a report visual in edit mode, using its context menu to mark it as a verified answer, and then defining multiple trigger-phrase variants so Copilot recognizes both exact and paraphrased versions of the same question.

Writing a description for every single column indiscriminately, rather than focusing on the fields that matter for common questions, is flagged as a practitioner antipattern that produces shallow descriptions without improving Copilot's answer quality.
Recommended practice after applying Prep data for AI changes is to wait some minutes before retesting, since updates to the model are not guaranteed to be reflected in Copilot answers immediately.
Per Microsoft's own documentation, the classic Q&A visual and related Q&A experiences in Power BI are being deprecated, with Microsoft recommending Copilot as the natural-language successor.
A model-level diagnostic feature, described in the post as 'How Copilot Arrived At This,' can be inspected on Copilot answers to help authors troubleshoot why a response was generated the way it was.

Per Microsoft's documentation, Copilot for Power BI requires the underlying semantic model to reside in a workspace backed by paid Fabric or Power BI Premium capacity, and requires a tenant admin to have Copilot enabled for the organization.
